title: k-Wise Independent Hashing for Honey Encryption
summary: Random-oracle or ideal-cipher models permit independent ball placement; it remains open whether k-wise independent hashing gives strong honey-encryption security in many cases.

formal_statement.body: For the honey-encryption approach using a good DTE designed from an estimate of the target message distribution, message-recovery security reduces to analyzing the balls-and-bins game induced by the particular key and message distributions; random-oracle or ideal-cipher modeling permits independent ball placement. Determine whether $k$-wise independent hashing, and therefore $k$-wise independent ball placement, can also provide strong message-recovery security in many such cases.

scope.domain: Honey-encryption message-recovery security analyzed through DTE-induced balls-and-bins games and limited-independence hashing.
assumptions: The honey-encryption approach uses a good DTE designed from an estimate of the target message distribution.
The independent-ball-placement baseline uses random-oracle or ideal-cipher modeling.
parameters: k: level of independence in the hash family and corresponding ball placement
Key and message distributions: induce the balls-and-bins game being analyzed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether k-wise independent hashing, and thus k-wise independent ball placement, provides strong message-recovery security in many such cases.

citations.label: Honey Encryption: Security Beyond the Brute-Force Bound

progress.summary: The source presents independent ball placement under random-oracle or ideal-cipher modeling as the baseline for the DTE-induced balls-and-bins analysis. It explicitly conjectures that k-wise independence may provide strong security in many cases.
citation_labels: Ari Juels et al., Honey Encryption: Security Beyond the Brute-Force Bound
